# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 32 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 32 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_032_page_001.jpg

---

## Mandate 4, Chapter 2 — Post-Baptismal Repentance

**1** I pressed him again: "Sir, I've heard some teachers say that there's no repentance except the one we received at baptism — when we went under the water and all our past sins were forgiven. Is that really all we get?" **2** "That teaching is correct," he said, "as far as it goes. Yes — someone who has been forgiven should not go on sinning. They should live in purity. **3** But since you ask everything so thoroughly, let me show you more — though I want to be careful not to give an excuse for error to people who are just coming to faith or who have recently believed. People who are new to faith, or about to come to faith, don't get a second chance at repentance — they get a complete wiping clean of all past sins when they're baptized. **4** But for those who were called in earlier times — God established a specific provision of repentance for them. Why? Because God knows every heart and sees everything ahead of time. He knew how weak human beings are. He knew how many tricks the devil had to use against God's servants and how much damage he intended to do. **5** So in his great mercy, God had compassion on his creation and established this special repentance. And authority over this repentance was given to me. **6** But here is what I'm telling you clearly: if after receiving this great and holy calling someone is led by the devil into sin, that person has one repentance available to them. But if they keep sinning and keep repenting, cycling through it over and over — that helps them nothing. They will find it nearly impossible to live to God." **7** "I feel like I've come alive just hearing this explained clearly," I said. "I know now that if I stop adding to my sins, I will be saved." "Yes, you will," he said. "And so will everyone who does the same."

---

*PNEUMA note: This chapter's theological tension is real and consequential: it opens a door (one post-baptismal repentance) while simultaneously warning against presuming on that door (cycling sin-repentance is worthless). The Shepherd neither condemns post-baptismal sinners to permanent exclusion nor enables casual sinning.*
